newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close easier in thin flows.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close easier in thin flows.

text.p: Canada's bond market ended Monday weaker after sellers managed to gain the upper hand in thin flows.

"After a whirlwind of price activity last week, Canadian bonds started off this week on lighter volume," said Technical Data's Canadian market analyst Jeoff Hall in a market report. "With no essential economic releases or policy-maker remarks, the markets were left to drift lower in quiet trading."
On Monday Canada's 30-year benchmark bond slipped C$0.30 to C$111.00 to yield 7.071 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark, which traded flat to yield 6.82 percent.
The spread widened to 25 basis points from 23 at Friday's close.
Some investors left their desks for March school break.

"With the lack of flows, the path of least resistance was to the weak side," said one trader. Canada's bond market had surged on Friday amid U.S. investor relief that U.S. job growth in February was not stronger.

By comparison, Canadian February figures showed job losses. "Fortunately -- or unfortunately, depending on which side of the coin you're on -- Canada has no threat of runaway employment growth," Hall said.

This week in Canada there will be little economic data but the Bank of Canada will hold a two-year bond auction on Wednesday. The U.S. will see a slew of numbers, including Jnauary's wholesale trade and March 8 Johnson Redbook on Tuesday.

In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.00 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.25 to C$104.05 yielding 6.430 percent while the U.S. 10-year dipped 1/32 to yield 6.55 percent. The negative spread narrowed to 12 basis points from 14.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.97 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.19 percent.
